extra.message: Hardcoded weak Flask SECRET_KEY enables session forgery — Because the Flask session-signing secret is a hardcoded, guessable string ('random') committed to source, an attacker can forge arbitrary session cookies (e.g., set `loggedin` to any value) and bypass the /login authentication boundary entirely to access /confidential. [verified: SECRET_KEY='random' is hardcoded and trivial, letting an attacker forge signed session cookies to set loggedin truthy and bypass /login entirely.]

Hardcoded/weak Flask SECRET_KEY enabling session forgery — Attacker can forge a validly-signed session cookie (e.g., set loggedin truthy) and bypass authentication on /confidential without ever logging in [verified: Duplicate of finding 0 — same hardcoded weak SECRET_KEY enabling session cookie forgery and auth bypass.]

Server-Side Template Injection in 404 handler via request.url — Attacker crafts a URL whose path contains a Jinja expression (e.g. referencing `system_call` context function from Monitoring.py) that gets rendered and evaluated, enabling arbitrary Jinja expression execution and, combined with the system_call context processor, remote code execution. [verified: request.url is embedded via .format() into a raw string that is then passed to render_template_string, so Jinja parses attacker-controlled path/query content as template syntax, enabling SSTI/RCE with no sanitization.]

Insecure pickle deserialization leads to RCE — Attacker submits a malicious pickle payload (as hex) which executes arbitrary code via `__reduce__` upon `pickle.load`, achieving remote code execution. [verified: request.form['data_obj'] is hex-decoded and pickle.load()'d with no auth, allow-list, or integrity check, giving direct RCE via crafted __reduce__ payload.]

Insecure YAML deserialization leads to RCE — Attacker-controlled YAML deserialization can execute arbitrary code on the server (classic PyYAML unsafe load RCE). [verified: yaml.load(yaml_file) is called without a SafeLoader, and yaml_file is base64-decoded directly from the attacker-controlled /information/<input> URL segment with no sanitization, allowing arbitrary object construction via !!python/object tags.]

Hardcoded default credentials and Flask debug mode enabled — Trivial brute-force/guessing of admin/admin grants authenticated access; combined with app.debug=True, any triggered exception exposes the Werkzeug debugger allowing arbitrary code execution. [verified: Login.py:12 hardcodes admin/admin with no rate limiting, and project/__init__.py:6 sets app.debug=True unconditionally, enabling the Werkzeug debugger/console on unhandled exceptions.]

Path traversal / arbitrary file read via getXML — Attacker can read arbitrary files on the server filesystem readable by the app process (e.g., source code, credentials, Database.db). [verified: fileName is taken directly from request.form with zero sanitization and passed to open()/send_file(), allowing arbitrary file read via traversal.]

Authentication bypass via unconditional session assignment in Webmaster route — Any anonymous visitor can obtain a 'loggedin' session by simply hitting /webmaster, then access /confidential without ever knowing valid credentials [verified: Webmaster.py:12 sets session['loggedin'] to a fresh uuid on any GET/POST with no credential check, and Confidential.py grants access purely on truthiness of session['loggedin'], so hitting /webmaster then /confidential bypasses auth entirely.]

SQL Injection in Dashboard page lookup — Attacker can read/modify arbitrary data in the SQLite database, including the users table with password hashes, via UNION-based SQLi through the pageId path segment. [verified: pageId flows directly from the URL path into a string-concatenated SQL query with no sanitization or parameterization, enabling classic UNION-based SQLi to dump the users table.]

Werkzeug debug mode enabled and exposed on all interfaces — Remote attacker triggering any unhandled exception can access the Werkzeug interactive debugger, potentially achieving remote code execution [verified: app.debug=True is set unconditionally and runserver.py binds to 0.0.0.0, exposing the unauthenticated Werkzeug interactive debugger (RCE) to any remote client on an unhandled exception.]

CORS misconfiguration allowing credentialed cross-origin access — A malicious website can make credentialed cross-origin requests to /confidential and read the authenticated response, exfiltrating sensitive session-bound data. [verified: runserver.py sets CORS(app, resources={r"/*": {"origins": "*"}}) applying to all routes including /confidential, which explicitly sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, allowing any origin to make credentialed requests and read the authenticated response.]

Missing authentication on messaging endpoints — Anonymous attacker can read all stored messages and post arbitrary content/links to all users [verified: Neither /messaging nor /messaging/new checks session['loggedin'], unlike Confidential.py, so any anonymous user can read stored messages and insert arbitrary name/message/link content via storeMessages.]

XXE in XML validator upload — Attacker can define external entities to read arbitrary local files or trigger SSRF/DoS (billion laughs) via crafted XML uploaded to /validator/upload. [verified: pulldom.parseString has no DTD/entity restrictions applied and directly parses user-supplied XML with output reflected via toxml(), enabling XXE.]

Unrestricted/unsanitized file upload with path traversal in filename — Attacker can write files outside the intended uploads directory via a crafted filename (e.g. `../../project/controllers/evil.py` or overwrite existing files), or upload an .html file later served to victims for stored XSS. [verified: file.save uses raw client-supplied filename (no secure_filename/path stripping) concatenated into 'uploads/'+filename, allowing path traversal writes and .html upload for stored XSS.]
